I call myself an "ex-addict." Of course I remain sober and I no longer use porn, alcohol, pot, pills, or gamble. If I started using those things again, I'm sure addiction would rear it's ugly head again. BUT - I think labeling myself an "addict for life" (as some schools of thought in recovery do) is disempowering. Or, at least, it is for me. So, I don't do it.

When I attended 12-step meetings a couple years back (when I was first feeling my way around in the recovery world) it was definitely a weird thing to not call myself an addict. Everyone else would do the "hi, I'm X and I'm an addict" or "I'm Y and I'm an alcoholic." I would just go, "Hi, I'm LiferingMod." No one hassled me about it, but it felt weird. When I ended up in Lifering Secular Recovery, it felt a lot better.

I don't think the business of not labeling myself has really hampered my recovery at all. I just don't think it matters much either way. Which is good - because my life was pretty bad before.
